## Today's NFL transactions briefing

### Free agent signings
- **Texans signed Kenneth Murray, Jr.** — Adds veteran depth and a new competition piece for Houston’s defensive rotation.
- **Dolphins signed Jaylin Simpson** — A depth move that gives Miami another developmental defensive back.
- **Ravens signed Chris Moore** — Brings in a familiar veteran receiver for depth and special teams help.
- **Jaguars signed Jack Kiser** — Adds linebacker depth and competition on defense.
- **Giants signed Josh Tupou** — Bolsters the interior defensive line rotation.
- **Texans signed Jamal Hill** — Another depth add for Houston’s defense.
- **Falcons signed Nick Muse** — Adds tight end depth; likely a role-player move.
- **Vikings signed DeeJay Dallas** — Gives Minnesota another backfield option and return-game versatility.
- **Cardinals signed Kalen King** — Adds a young defensive back to the secondary mix.
- **Commanders signed Lucas Patrick** — Provides veteran offensive line depth.
- **49ers signed KhaDarel Hodge** — Adds experienced receiver depth and special teams value.

### Practice squad moves
- **Titans signed Jimmy Ciarlo to the practice squad** — Depth stash with development upside.
- **Dolphins signed Cal Adomitis to the practice squad** — Likely strengthens the specialist pipeline.
- **Ravens signed Amani Oruwariye to the practice squad** — Veteran corner depth for insurance and evaluation.

- **Falcons signed Khalil Herbert to the practice squad** — Backfield depth; worth watching if injuries open a path.
- **Packers signed Eric Johnson to the practice squad** — Adds defensive line depth.
- **Vikings signed Jerome Ford to the practice squad** — A notable backfield depth addition.
- **Cardinals signed Jerrick Reed II to the practice squad** — Secondary depth and development.
- **Commanders signed Marvin Jones Jr. to the practice squad** — Veteran receiver depth.
- **49ers signed Jack Stoll to the practice squad** — Tight end depth with roster flexibility.

### Reserve/Injured placements
- **Dolphins placed Kyle Louis on reserve/injured** — Removes a depth piece from the active mix for now.
- **Falcons placed Da’Shawn Hand on reserve/injured** — Hurts Atlanta’s defensive line depth.
- **Jaguars placed BJ Green II on reserve/injured** — Opens a hole in the pass-rush/depth rotation.
- **Cardinals placed Kitan Crawford on reserve/injured** — Secondary depth loss.
- **Commanders placed Jordan Magee on reserve/injured** — Defensive depth setback.
- **Chiefs placed Cooper McDonald on reserve/injured** — Reduces Kansas City’s depth options.

### Waiver terminations
- **Panthers terminated Jimmy Horn Jr. via waivers** — Clears a roster spot; his status is now uncertain.
- **Cowboys terminated Israel Abanikanda via waivers** — Dallas moves on from a depth back.
- **Packers terminated Trey Dean III via waivers** — Opens a spot in the secondary.

### Quick read
- Biggest themes: **depth churn, practice-squad promotions, and injury-related roster shuffling**.
- Fantasy impact is mostly **minimal** unless one of the backfield/receiver moves opens a clearer path later.

### Today’s injury briefing

**Steelers**
- RT **Troy Fautanu** (ankle) was a **non-participant**.
- TE **Darnell Washington** (NIR/personal) was a **non-participant**.
- WR **Michael Pittman Jr.** (foot) was **limited**.
- **Why it matters:** Pittsburgh’s offense is already dealing with early-week attrition up front and at tight end before Week 2.

**Lions**
- **Christian Mahogany** (hip) and rookie RT **Blake Miller** (knee) were **ruled out** vs. the Bills.
- CB **D.J. Reed** is **questionable**.
- **Why it matters:** Detroit’s offensive line is taking a real hit for a key road game in Buffalo.

**Saints**
- LS **Zach Wood** has a **Grade 2 calf strain** and is expected to miss **4-6 weeks**.
- **Why it matters:** Mostly a special teams issue, but it’s a longer absence.

**Dolphins**
- EDGE **Chop Robinson** is in the **concussion protocol**.
- **Malik Willis** is dealing with a **toe injury**.
- **Why it matters:** Robinson’s status is the bigger one to monitor; concussion protocol often means uncertainty into game week.

**49ers**
- WR **De’Zhaun Stribling** had ankle surgery and is expected to miss about **10 weeks**.
- TE **Jake Tonges** needs MCL surgery and is **out for the season**.
- **Why it matters:** San Francisco’s depth at tight end and receiver is getting thinner fast.

**Jets / Packers**
- S **Minkah Fitzpatrick** missed practice and is **week-to-week** with a groin injury.
- **Why it matters:** He looks unlikely to be available before Week 3.

**Seahawks**
- QB **Sam Darnold** is reportedly **more day-to-day than week-to-week** with his glute injury.
- **Why it matters:** That’s the clearest sign of the day pointing toward a potential near-term return.

### Returning-from-injury watch
- No player was officially confirmed back in the available reports.
- **Sam Darnold** is the closest to a return based on the updated wording.

- **Zay Flowers (WR)** — Flowers was out of Wednesday practice with the hamstring issue after leaving Week 1, and ESPN is flagging Rashod Bateman as the Ravens’ receiver to watch in Week 2. If Flowers is limited or inactive, Baltimore’s pass-game volume likely shifts toward Bateman, with Devontez Walker also available after a full practice. [4, 6, 9]

- **Declan Doyle / Ravens offense** — Baltimore is part of the leaguewide move back under center, and the new offensive staff has been tied to that trend. That points to more under-center structure and play-action-friendly sequencing this week, which can change how the Ravens distribute rushing and passing volume versus a shotgun-heavy script. [1]

- **Baltimore game plan** — The Ravens are being described as hunting explosive plays on offense while the defense is willing to sell out to prevent them, suggesting a more boom-or-bust approach than pure volume. For DFS/fantasy, that supports upside for Baltimore’s main playmakers but also adds weekly volatility if chunk gains don’t hit. [2]

- **Trey Hendrickson (OLB)** — Baltimore used Hendrickson as a straightforward edge weapon in Week 1, giving him roughly 25 dedicated pass-rush snaps without needing exotic deployment. If he suits up, his role keeps the Ravens’ sack pressure and D/ST ceiling tied to a concentrated edge threat rather than scheme tricks. [3, 6]

That preserves his flex/DFS appeal as a viable secondary target in a game that could still feature a healthy target share. [6, 7]

- **Bryce Young (QB)** — His Week 1 line of 361 passing yards and three touchdowns suggests Carolina’s offense can support real quarterback volume, not just low-end game-manager production. That keeps Young viable as a streamer and raises the ceiling on the Panthers’ pass catchers if this matchup stays competitive. [3]

- **Michael Penix Jr./Falcons QB situation** — Atlanta still hasn’t settled its Week 2 starter, with Penix saying he’s close but not fully ready and the starting job likely his once healthy. That adds some uncertainty to the game environment and makes Carolina’s play volume and efficiency a little harder to project until Atlanta’s QB is confirmed. [2, 9, 10]

- **Jordan Love (QB, GB)** — Green Bay’s Week 1 protection issues weren’t limited to the offensive line; tight end Mark Redman and running back Chris Brooks also missed in pass protection. That keeps the Jets’ sack/pressure ceiling elevated and slightly improves NYJ DST and turnover outlook while making Love less efficient. [1]

- **Jason Sanders (K)** — The Jets’ kicking situation still looks shaky: Sanders made 3 of 4 attempts last week, missed a 54-yarder, and the staff may still look elsewhere if the inconsistency continues. That keeps the Jets kicker spot volatile and lowers confidence in fantasy field-goal volume this week. [3]

SF.summary:
- **De'Zhaun Stribling (WR)** — He was placed on IR after ankle surgery and is expected to miss about 10 weeks. For Week 2, that opens snaps and targets for the remaining receiver rotation, with Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson next up and Jacob Cowing the most likely volume beneficiary if he can hold the role. [2, 3]

- **Connor Colby (LG) / 49ers offensive line** — Colby got the start at left guard in Week 1 and the line held up well, with no blocker allowing more than two pressures. That supports Brock Purdy’s efficiency and keeps the run game on track against Miami, a small boost to SF skill-position projections. [5]

- **49ers travel/recovery** — After the Australia trip, the team got five days of rest and is back into a normal weekly routine, with players noting the jet-lag adjustment is behind them. For Week 2, that lowers any concern about fatigue depressing usage or efficiency for the core starters. [1]

PIT.summary:
- **Troy Fautanu (OT)** — The Steelers’ starting left tackle missed Wednesday with an ankle issue after briefly leaving Week 1 before returning. If he’s limited or inactive, Pittsburgh’s pass protection and left-side run blocking get shakier, which would depress efficiency for the passing game and the backs this week. [2, 3]

- **Patriots CB Carlton Davis III** — Davis stayed sidelined and played almost every snap last week, so New England’s secondary could be missing one of its main boundary pieces. That softens the matchup for Pittsburgh’s perimeter pass catchers and slightly raises the Steelers’ QB/WR/TE ceiling. [1]

- **Joey Porter Jr. (CB)** — Porter was limited again, now for conditioning, and was expected to do more in practice than he did last week. If he still isn’t at full strength, Pittsburgh’s top boundary coverage could be compromised, which improves the Patriots’ passing outlook and trims the Steelers D/ST ceiling. [2, 3]

WAS.summary:
- **Dorance Armstrong (LB)** — ESPN says Armstrong is set to return for Week 2 against Dallas after being limited in Wednesday’s report. That gives Washington back an edge-rush piece, which should help the Commanders’ sack/pressure outlook and slightly improve the defense’s fantasy ceiling this week. [7, 8]

- **Frankie Luvu (LB)** — Luvu did not practice Wednesday, and Washington already has Jordan Magee on IR, so the linebacker rotation is thinner than it was in Week 1. If Luvu can’t play, Washington’s tackle and snap volume at linebacker would have to be redistributed, but today’s items do not specify the replacement plan. [1, 6, 7]

- **Chig Okonkwo (TE)** — Okonkwo also did not practice Wednesday with a hamstring issue. If he’s limited or out, Washington’s TE usage would need to be spread elsewhere, but the reports do not name a clear beneficiary, so his status mainly suppresses the position’s certainty for DFS/fantasy. [1, 6, 7]

- **Antonio Williams** — Williams only touched the ball four times in the opener, but he was Washington’s most efficient receiver per target and its highest-graded offensive player. That keeps a role expansion on the table if the staff rewards efficiency, but today’s items do not specify any added workload for Week 2. [1]

NE.summary:
- **A.J. Brown (WR)** — Brown is expected to miss about six weeks, forcing New England to redistribute Week 2 targets. Chad Graff says Kyle Williams could get more involved, and Mack Hollins’ established chemistry with Drake Maye gives him a clearer intermediate role; the offense may also lean more on the run game. That makes the passing tree thinner and more volatile for Maye’s projection. [1, 7]

- **TreVeyon Henderson (RB)** — Henderson is tracking to play after missing the opener, which would add a live backfield option back into the mix. If he’s active, he can siphon touches from the other Patriots runners and make the workload split less predictable; the exact division is not specified. [6, 12]

- **Will Campbell (OT)** — Campbell framed the Steelers’ T.J. Watt and Cameron Heyward as a major pass-protection test and stressed consistency up front. If that pressure shows up, it can cap Drake Maye’s efficiency and keep New England’s passing game on the fragile side for DFS purposes. [2]

- **Juwan Johnson (TE)** — Johnson did not practice Wednesday, while Oscar Delp was limited, so the Saints’ TE usage is less stable than usual. That clouds the position’s target projection and makes it harder to trust a meaningful pass-game role there this week. [2]

- **Cam Jordan (DE)** — Jordan was limited with a hamstring, which could keep New Orleans’ pass rush from being at full strength. That slightly improves Baltimore’s offensive outlook and makes the Saints DST a shakier fantasy play. [2]

IND.summary:
- **Daniel Jones (QB)** — Week 1 was a rough passing debut: Jones finished near the bottom of the league in several key measures, and Indianapolis struggled to consistently move the ball through the air. For Week 2, that keeps the Colts’ passing game a little more fragile and lowers confidence in the ceiling of IND pass-catchers until Jones shows better efficiency [1].

- **The Colts’ WR1** — Indianapolis’ newest top receiving option spent most of the offseason working back from a clean-up, and the initial Week 2 injury report says his role is still worth monitoring. If he’s not fully ramped, target share may stay more spread out than usual, which would cap the upside of the whole receiving tree [2].

- **Chiefs’ front/coverage health** — Kansas City’s DT Chris Jones opened the week limited, while CB Mansoor Delane was full after leaving Week 1 early. If Jones is less than 100 percent, that’s the one Chiefs note that could slightly help IND’s protection and run efficiency, but Mahomes and Rashee Rice were full participants, so the matchup still looks tough overall [5].

- **Akeem Davis-Gaither (LB) / Cam Bynum (S)** — Indianapolis is moving the defensive green-dot duties from Bynum to Davis-Gaither after the Week 1 collapse. That’s mainly a defensive communication fix, but it could stabilize IND’s defense enough to matter for the Colts DST outlook this week [3, 6].
